questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was really easy to socialize with the local students, as each team included at least one of them. They were very helpful and gave us great advice about the hidden gems of the city. Thanks to their support, it was also much easier to orient ourselves around the university

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the older local people couldn't talk in english

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality—especially from the local students, the history, the architecture and the pastries were truly memorable.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: They will enjoy the experience, gain valuable knowledge and skills, and should definitely try to socialize with all the students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They should be careful of pickpockets and avoid potentially unsafe areas of Paris, such as Saint-Denis

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining knowledge and meeting students and teachers from three different countries was a valuable part of the experience

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exchange was only five days long, so the biggest challenge was making the most of a limited time — balancing learning, networking, and exploring the city

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
